summary: The lease should provide specific contact details for repair emergencies.
explanation: Your lease should include contact information for reporting repairs, especially for emergencies. Without this, you might not know who to contact when urgent issues arise.
compliant_examples: For emergency repairs, contact the landlord at 01-123-4567
Maintenance issues should be reported to maintenance@property.com
For urgent repairs, call the property manager at the number provided
non_compliant_examples: No mention of how to report maintenance issues
recommended_action: Ask your landlord to provide specific contact details for reporting repairs and emergencies. This should include a phone number that can be reached outside of normal business hours for urgent issues.

summary: The lease should mention that the tenancy will be registered with the RTB.
explanation: Your landlord is legally required to register your tenancy with the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB). This registration provides important protections for both tenants and landlords.
compliant_examples: This tenancy will be registered with the RTB as required by law
The landlord will register this tenancy with the Residential Tenancies Board
This tenancy is subject to registration under the Residential Tenancies Act
non_compliant_examples: No reference to the Residential Tenancies Board
recommended_action: Ask your landlord to confirm that the tenancy will be registered with the RTB and to provide you with the registration confirmation once completed.

summary: The lease should state your right to peaceful and exclusive occupation.
explanation: Your lease should explicitly state your right to peaceful and exclusive occupation of the property. This means your landlord cannot interfere with your enjoyment of the property through frequent visits or other disturbances.
compliant_examples: The tenant has the right to peaceful and exclusive occupation of the property
The landlord guarantees the tenant's right to quiet enjoyment of the premises
The tenant shall have peaceful enjoyment of the dwelling without interference
non_compliant_examples: No reference to tenant's right to privacy
recommended_action: Ask your landlord to include a clause that explicitly states your right to peaceful and exclusive occupation of the property.

summary: The lease should specify how and when rent reviews will occur.
explanation: Your lease should clearly state how and when rent reviews will occur. In Rent Pressure Zones, rent can only be reviewed once every 12 months and increases are capped.
compliant_examples: Rent may be reviewed once every 12 months with 90 days' written notice
Any rent increase will be communicated with at least 90 days' notice
Rent reviews will follow RTB guidelines and provide required notice
non_compliant_examples: No mention of rent review process
No reference to notice period for rent increases
No information about frequency of rent reviews
recommended_action: Ask your landlord to include a clause that specifies how and when rent reviews will occur, in compliance with current rental laws.

summary: The lease should mention an inventory of the property's contents.
explanation: Your lease should mention that an inventory report will be completed at the start of the tenancy. This inventory should list all items provided with the property and their condition.
compliant_examples: An inventory and condition report will be completed and signed by both parties
The condition of the property is documented in the attached inventory report
A detailed inventory forms part of this agreement
non_compliant_examples: No reference to property condition documentation
recommended_action: Ask your landlord to conduct an inventory check with you at the start of the tenancy and to provide you with a copy of the inventory report.
